title: When the Garden Sings
premise: Quentin Iversen has spent fifteen years as the reluctant warden of a sealed gate between the human city of Vell and the fading realm of Everwood, selling harmless charms while pretending magic died long ago. When a child named Ash arrives at his door speaking the First Tongue, Quentin realizes the gate is failing and the last dragon-fire that sustains both worlds is guttering out. Hunted by the Ministry of Unmaking and shadowed by the ghost of the mentor he betrayed, Quentin and Ash must gather three scattered covenant-keepers—each of whom lost something to him—to reforge the broken pact. In the end, Quentin must surrender his own memories of the fifteen years he spent guarding the gate, giving them to the fire so it can burn again; he survives, but no longer remembers why the child at his door calls him family.
about_author: Oscar Zhou is the pen name of a former botanist who traded field notebooks for fantasy manuscripts after a decade cataloguing endangered orchids. They write about doors, debts, and the people who keep both.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller's Hours
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A day in his cramped shop in outlawed-magic Vell: selling luck-knots and fever-charms, dodging Ministry inspectors, and checking the hidden gate beneath his floorboards each night. Establishes his loneliness and rigid routines. Emotional beat: quiet dread—he counts the days since the gate last hummed, and the number frightens him.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On the eve of the winter census, a barefoot child appears at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom—and every ward on the house answers aloud. The child, Ash, carries a dragon-scale pendant that burns cold. Emotional beat: terror curdling into recognition, because Quentin knows the words even though he swore he'd forgotten them.

chapters.title: What the Ministry Burns
chapters.summary: Ash's POV, fragmented and dreamlike. Ash flees through Vell's memory: a village unmade overnight, a mother who spoke the same old words, inspectors with white gloves collecting names. Ash followed rumors of 'the keeper' for a year. Emotional beat: desperate hope meeting a stranger who flinches at the sight of them.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Interrogating Ash over soup, Quentin pieces together the truth: the covenant between realms is fraying, and Ash is its living seal—a child born across the threshold. Flashbacks reveal Quentin's betrayal of his mentor, Wren, during the gate's original closing. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing like a drowned thing.

chapters.title: The Inspector with White Gloves
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Ministry Inspector Corvane arrives, courteous and terrible, asking about 'unregistered resonance.' Quentin lies well but not well enough; Corvane leaves a listening-sigil behind. Quentin decides they must flee before dawn. Emotional beat: the sick clarity of a man whose careful life just ended.

chapters.title: Down Through the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Quentin and Ash's alternating POV. They escape through the gate itself—which opens onto a dying Everwood: grey orchards, rivers running backward, a sky the color of ash. The dragon-fire mountain on the horizon flickers like a dying lamp. Emotional beat: awe and grief; home was never home, and exile was never exile.

chapters.title: The Orchard That Remembers
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. In an orchard where trees store memories instead of fruit, Ash touches a bough and experiences Quentin's past—the night the covenant broke, Wren's face, Quentin's choice to save himself. Ash says nothing, but begins to fear the man guiding them. Emotional beat: the first crack of trust.

chapters.title: The Bridge-Keeper of Sorrow Ford
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. First covenant-keeper: Maren, a ferry-woman who holds the covenant's river-stone and hasn't spoken since her voice was taken as payment decades ago. She communicates through the water, which shows truths. She agrees to help—but only if Quentin confesses what he did to Wren. Emotional beat: shame made public.

chapters.title: Confession at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin tells the river everything: fifteen years ago, the covenant demanded a keeper give up what they loved most, and Quentin let Wren take his place rather than lose his memories. The river accepts the truth; Maren gives up her stone. Emotional beat: catharsis that doesn't feel like forgiveness.

chapters.title: Corvane Crosses Over
chapters.summary: Inspector Corvane's POV. Corvane follows through the gate using the listening-sigil, revealing the Ministry's true purpose: not eradicating magic, but harvesting the covenant's power to make Vell immortal and Everwood dead. Corvane believes this is mercy. Emotional beat: chilling conviction—an antagonist who thinks he's kind.

chapters.title: The Smith Who Hates Dragons
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Second covenant-keeper: Brannoc, a dwarven smith in the Cinderholds who forged the original covenant-chain and now refuses to help, blaming dragons for his daughter's death. Ash, carrying a dragon-scale, becomes an unlikely emissary. Emotional beat: anger met with a child's stubborn honesty.

chapters.title: Scale and Hammer
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Testing Ash's scale against forge-fire, Brannoc learns his daughter didn't die by dragonfire but protecting the fire-mountain from Ministry agents years ago. Grief redirects into purpose; he agrees to reforge the chain if they retrieve the third keeper. Emotional beat: rage transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The City That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The trio reaches Hollowmere, a city whose inhabitants traded their collective memory to the Ministry for safety—a preview of Corvane's promise for Vell. Among the blank-faced citizens moves the third keeper: Wren herself, alive, her name traded away. Emotional beat: hope and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren exists without identity, sustained by fragments of others' memories, yet something in Quentin's voice pulls at her. She doesn't know him, but she knows she hates being near him—or needs to be. Emotional beat: love persisting without memory, which is worse than grief.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. To restore Wren's self, someone must pay the covenant's price again: their most cherished memories. Quentin offers his fifteen years—all of them, including every moment that made his survival bearable. Wren, half-restored, must choose whether to accept a sacrifice from the man who betrayed her. Emotional beat: the cost of love priced in forgetting.

chapters.title: Corvane's Mercy
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane captures Ash, believing removing the 'living seal' will painlessly end both realms' suffering—Everwood dies, Vell lives forever. He offers Quentin a place in the new order. Quentin refuses; Corvane, genuinely puzzled, prepares the Unmaking. Emotional beat: two men, both certain they're saving someone.

chapters.title: Storming the Fire-Mountain
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The rescue: Maren's river floods the Ministry's siege lines, Brannoc's reforged chain sings, and Quentin walks into Corvane's camp unarmed to trade himself for Ash. Wren, remembering enough to be furious, strikes the blow that frees them all. Emotional beat: found family functioning as one instrument.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon-Fire
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. At the mountain's heart, the ancient dragon Ember-that-Waits lies nearly extinguished. Ash, the living seal, understands at last: the fire doesn't need fuel—it needs a story worth burning for, held in memory. The covenant must be spoken in the First Tongue, by someone who belongs to both worlds. Emotional beat: a child accepting a weight no adult would hand them.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Climax. As Corvane's forces breach the mountain, the keepers join hands around the fire: Maren's stone, Brannoc's chain, Wren's restored voice, Ash's tongue, Quentin's memories poured into the flame. The covenant blazes back to life; Corvane, offered a share of the new fire, chooses instead to kneel—weeping, unmade of his certainty. Emotional beat: sacrifice as an act of joy.

chapters.title: What Quentin Cannot Remember
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The price is paid: Quentin lives, whole and healthy, but the last fifteen years are gone. He looks at Ash and Wren as strangers. Wren, who once lost everything to his cowardice, now chooses to stay and teach him who he was. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness—love rebuilt from scratch.

chapters.title: Two Doors, Both Open
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Months later: the shop reopens, now selling real charms openly; the gate stands open, guarded by choice rather than law. Ash splits time between worlds, carrying letters and dragonfruit. Quentin asks Ash, gently, how they met. Emotional beat: warmth earned through loss; beginnings disguised as endings.

chapters.title: When the Garden Sings
chapters.summary: Ensemble finale. Spring comes to both realms at once. In the orchard of memories, a new tree grows bearing Quentin's returned memories—not restored to him, but shared: anyone may taste a season of his fifteen years. Wren reads one fruit and laughs for the first time. Emotional beat: memory as inheritance, not possession; the garden sings because it is finally tended together.
